reports.heading: Chicago, Illinois — LARGE STRONG-MAYOR / ALDERMANIC FAMILY
reports.name: Chicago
reports.text:
Verified institutional/room facts:
- Chicago City Council meetings normally begin at 10:00 a.m. in the Council Chambers on the second floor of City Hall, 121 N. LaSalle Street.
- The Office of the City Clerk publishes the current 2023–2027 Rules of Order and Procedure.
- Under those rules, the Mayor is the Presiding Officer of Council; the rules also provide President Pro Tempore, Assistant President Pro Tempore and Vice-Mayor succession for presiding duties.
- The Rules expressly contemplate chamber clearing, member recognition, points of order and other floor behavior. These are procedural scene mechanics, not background flavor.
- City Clerk infrastructure separately publishes Council reports/minutes, public-comment rules, executive orders, budgets and code/administrative-rule material.

reports.heading: Springfield, Illinois — MEDIUM CAPITAL-CITY MAYOR/ALDERMANIC FAMILY
reports.name: Springfield
reports.text:

- Springfield City Council and Committee of the Whole meetings are held in City Council Chambers, Room 301, on the third floor of Municipal Center West, 300 S. Seventh Street.

- Rules distinguish regular, special, adjourned and executive sessions and adopt Robert's Rules of Order for questions not covered by the local rules.
- Special meetings can be called by the Mayor or three Council members, require written subject notice and generally at least 48 hours notice.
- The same chamber is reused by administrative hearings and multiple boards/commissions. That makes it a general municipal civic-hearing room as well as a legislative room.
- Public-address rules require advance filing for ordinary Council comment with defined exceptions, which can affect how a public-meeting scene actually unfolds.

reports.heading: Detroit, Michigan — STRONG-MAYOR + DISTRICT/AT-LARGE COUNCIL + CIVIC-OVERSIGHT ECOSYSTEM
reports.name: Detroit
reports.text:
Verified institutional/room facts:
- Detroit has nine City Council members: seven geographic district members and two at-large members, each serving four-year terms.
- The city's budget materials describe Council as the legislative/oversight body and provide for a two-thirds override of a mayoral budget veto.
- The Coleman A. Young Municipal Center at 2 Woodward Avenue houses Council operations on the 13th floor.
- The Erma L. Henderson Auditorium, Suite 1300/13th floor, is an active public-hearing and commission room in 2026, used by the Historic District Commission and other civic proceedings.
- The 13th floor also includes a Committee of the Whole room used by municipal bodies.
- Detroit's 2012 Charter creates an unusually rich set of persistent civic actors around Council, including district-linked Community Advisory Councils and an eleven-member Board of Police Commissioners with seven elected district members plus four mayoral appointees confirmed by Council.
- A 2026 Council budget resolution explicitly proposes museum-quality art/photography displays in 13th-floor Council areas. If implemented, this is exactly the kind of temporally sourced civic-art layer the game's modular decoration system should support rather than treating as permanent architecture.


Scene families:
1. ERMA L. HENDERSON AUDITORIUM / large civic-hearing chamber.
2. 13TH-FLOOR COMMITTEE OF THE WHOLE room.
3. CITY COUNCIL MEMBER/OFFICE family on the 13th floor.
4. MAYOR/EXECUTIVE offices in CAYMC.
5. COMMUNITY ADVISORY COUNCIL neighborhood-meeting family, often outside central City Hall.

reports.heading: Grand Rapids, Michigan — COMMISSION-MANAGER FAMILY
reports.name: Grand Rapids
reports.text:
Verified institutional/room facts:
- Grand Rapids voters adopted the Commission-Manager form in 1916; the City Commission is the elected legislative/policymaking body and hires the City Manager, who is the chief administrator supervising city departments.
- The legislative body consists of the at-large Mayor plus six Commissioners, two elected from each of three wards.
- The Mayor is the official head of the City and presides over Commission decision meetings, but day-to-day executive administration belongs to the City Manager.
- City Commission Chambers are on the ninth floor of City Hall, 300 Monroe Avenue NW. Official 2026 notices continue to identify the ninth-floor chamber.
- Other municipal bodies such as the Planning Commission also use the Commission Chambers for public hearings, while smaller preparatory/lunch meetings may use separate ninth-floor rooms.


Scene families:
1. 9TH-FLOOR CITY COMMISSION CHAMBERS.
2. COMMISSIONER/MAYOR office family.
3. CITY MANAGER executive-office family — institutionally distinct from the Mayor's political role.
4. CITY HALL committee/conference rooms.

reports.heading: Lincoln, Nebraska — HOME-RULE MAYOR-COUNCIL + SHARED COUNTY/CITY CIVIC ROOM
reports.name: Lincoln
reports.text:
Verified institutional/room facts:
- Lincoln is a Home Rule Charter city; city materials identify the charter as the city's local constitution subject to state constitutional/statutory limits.
- The charter establishes a Mayor-Council form.
- Council has seven members: four elected from districts and three at large.
- Full Council meets most Mondays in the City Council Chambers of the County/City Building, 555 S. 10th Street; the chamber is on the first floor.
- Council has explicit authority to make laws, approve budgets and audit City agencies.
- The same chamber hosts the joint Lincoln-Lancaster County Planning Commission, city/county zoning boards and interlocal bodies, making it a useful shared-government environment rather than a room belonging only to Council.
- Planning Commission decisions can be either final or recommendatory and can be appealed to City Council or County Board depending on the item. This creates real institutional handoffs within the same physical civic complex.

1. COUNTY/CITY BUILDING COUNCIL CHAMBERS — shared municipal/county public-hearing room.

reports.text:

- Council Chambers is Room 300 on the third floor; Council-member offices and Clerk of Council are also on the third floor.
- The current 2026 Council contact list identifies weekly Wednesday Council sessions in Room 300.
- Council adopts its Rules under City Charter authority. Current rules distinguish Council Chamber, meetings, presiding officer, conduct of business, motions, ordinances/resolutions and committees.
- The Mayor presides over Council meetings but is not a Council member and does not vote on Council items under the city's current structure; the City Manager remains a separate administrative actor.

reports.heading: Louisville-Jefferson County, Kentucky — CONSOLIDATED METRO + HISTORIC CITY HALL
reports.name: Louisville-Jefferson County
reports.text:
Verified governance and room facts:
- Louisville and Jefferson County merged into Louisville Metro Government in 2003. Current Metro documents identify a mayor-council consolidated form with 26 Council districts and 26 district-elected Council members.
- Historic City Hall at 601 W. Jefferson Street houses Metro Council offices and chambers. The building was constructed 1870–73 in an Italianate stone civic style with period exterior sculptural/industrial motifs.
- Metro Council's own 2026 Art in City Hall program demonstrates that public-space decoration is temporally variable: local artwork is selected annually and displayed in the lobby, hallways and public areas rather than being permanent institutional architecture.
- Current Council policies explicitly distinguish Council staff, Clerk functions and consolidated-government executive units.


Scene families:
1. LOUISVILLE METRO COUNCIL CHAMBER — historic-city-hall legislative family.
2. METRO COUNCIL MEMBER/OFFICE family in Historic City Hall.
3. FIRST-FLOOR CONFERENCE / smaller civic-meeting family.
4. MAYOR / Metro executive-office family — research separately rather than assuming it occupies the Council's historic room family.
5. TEMPORARY/ROTATING ART layer tied to the annual Art in City Hall exhibition.


Simulation implication: consolidated Louisville should not spawn separate independent Louisville city and Jefferson County executive/legislative governments for functions that merger law consolidated. The 26 districts and council structure are legal/institutional facts, while rotating local artwork belongs to the temporal personalization/civic-art layer.

reports.heading: Lexington-Fayette, Kentucky — MERGED URBAN-COUNTY GOVERNMENT + ACTIVE GOVERNMENT-CENTER TRANSITION
reports.name: Lexington-Fayette
reports.text:

- Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government is a merged urban-county government. The Urban County Council is its legislative branch.
- Council has 15 members: 12 district members plus three countywide at-large seats; the highest-vote at-large member becomes Vice Mayor under the current system.
- Current Council meetings, work sessions and many public hearings occur in the second-floor Council Chamber at the Government Center, 200 E. Main Street. Smaller subcommittee work can occur in second-floor caucus or fifth-floor conference rooms.
- LFUCG is actively pursuing a replacement Government Center. On December 2, 2025 Council authorized P3 agreements to buy and redevelop the Truist Bank Building at 200 W. Vine Street as the future Government Center. The official project page includes a 2026 timeline and June 2026 Council update materials.
- The planned project consolidates offices now in the Government Center and Switow Building while coordinating with the Phoenix Building Development and Services Center.

reports.heading: Nashville-Davidson County, Tennessee — CONSOLIDATED METRO + LIVE 2026 COUNCIL-SIZE LITIGATION
reports.name: Nashville-Davidson County
reports.text:
Verified current facts:
- Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County is a consolidated city-county government effective April 1, 1963.
- Current Metro Council remains a 40-member legislative body: 35 district members and five at-large members; the Vice Mayor presides.
- Regular 2026 Council meetings are in the David Scobey Council Chambers at the Historic Metro Courthouse, 1 Public Square. The Metro Council Office is also in the Courthouse.
- Nashville's charter historically created separate General Services and Urban Services districts, which means consolidated geography does not imply one uniform service/tax layer.
- IMPORTANT TEMPORAL LEGAL STATE: a Tennessee statute seeking to cap metropolitan councils at 20 members is still being litigated. The Tennessee Supreme Court heard Metro's appeal February 12, 2026 and the docket shows supplemental briefing continuing through July 2026. Therefore 40 members is the current operational structure, while the future rule remains legally contested as of this research date.


Scene families:
1. DAVID SCOBEY COUNCIL CHAMBER — main full-Council/hearing family.
2. METRO COUNCIL OFFICE / Courthouse legislative-office family.
3. COURTHOUSE COMMITTEE/CLERK rooms immediately associated with the Council.
4. MAYOR executive-office family in the Historic Metro Courthouse.
5. SERVICE-DISTRICT/community settings when governance occurs outside the central building.


Simulation implication: institutional litigation can genuinely alter the size/representation structure of a legislature. Store the law, injunction/case state and effective outcome separately; do not pre-resolve the pending 2026 case.

reports.name: Austin
reports.text:

- Austin Charter establishes a council-manager form. Council is the legislative body; the Council-appointed City Manager runs day-to-day operations and implements ordinances.
- Since 2015 the elected structure is one at-large Mayor plus ten single-member geographic districts, created after the 2012 charter amendment. District boundaries are adjusted by an independent citizens redistricting commission after each census.
- Austin City Hall is at 301 W. 2nd Street. The City's own description emphasizes transparency, accessibility, informality, environmental sensitivity and technology as design goals.
- Completed in 2005 and designed by Antoine Predock, the building uses Texas limestone, recycled copper, a cascading waterfall and asymmetrical forms inspired by Austin-area waterways/canyons; it earned LEED Gold.
- The People’s Gallery occupies the first three floors as a recurring local/regional art exhibition. Current 2026 city material continues the program and accepts new exhibition applications. This is a strong example of civic decoration that should be time-versioned rather than baked permanently into a base texture.

reports.heading: Boston, Massachusetts — 13-MEMBER COUNCIL + LANDMARK BRUTALIST CITY HALL
reports.name: Boston
reports.text:
Verified current facts:
- Boston City Council has 13 members: nine district and four at-large members. The Mayor is the City's chief executive under the Charter.
- Current 2026 weekly Council meetings are held at noon in the Christopher A. Iannella Chamber on the fifth floor of Boston City Hall, unless otherwise noted. Committee hearings also use the Iannella Chamber.
- Boston City Hall opened in 1968 after a national design competition and was designed by Kallmann, McKinnell and Knowles. Official landmark documentation identifies it as a major work of American Brutalism using cast-in-place/precast concrete.
- The original design intentionally exposed different governmental functions in the architecture and carried brick paving from the plaza into the building to express public access. Boston formally moved to landmark the building, including significant interior public/civic elements.


Scene families:
1. IANNELLA COUNCIL CHAMBER — fifth-floor Brutalist legislative/hearing family.
2. COUNCIL OFFICE/COMMITTEE family on the fifth floor.

reports.text:
Current project authority: https://juneau.org/manager/cbj-municipal-offices
- Current regular Assembly location remains Assembly Chambers, Municipal Building, 155 Heritage Way until the actual move.
- CBJ is developing new municipal offices/Assembly Chambers in Michael J. Burns Building, 801 W. 10th Street.
- Planned new Assembly Chamber is materially larger than the existing chamber and is part of a broader move of roughly 147 personnel/public-service functions.
- Move anticipated in FY2027; actual occupancy/effective date must control scene switching.
Environment/game implication: `government seat` and recurring political room can change through a capital project. A 2026 world and later world may legitimately use different canonical Assembly environments.

reports.heading: Fairbanks city
reports.name: Fairbanks city
reports.text:
- Current City Council Chambers: 800 Cushman Street.
- City Council remains a separate incorporated-city government layer even though the area is also governed by Fairbanks North Star Borough.

reports.heading: Fairbanks North Star Borough
reports.name: Fairbanks North Star Borough
reports.text:
Official: https://www.fnsb.gov/415/Stay-Connected-with-the-Assembly
- Regular Assembly meetings: Mona Lisa Drexler Assembly Chambers, Juanita Helms Administration Center, 907 Terminal Street.
- Same room also supports Planning Commission, Platting Board, administrative hearings and other public bodies.
- Borough budgeting describes numerous individual taxing jurisdictions/service areas that do not erase the separate Cities of Fairbanks and North Pole.
- Current capital planning includes substantial Assembly-chamber dais/cabinet/technology reconfiguration.
Environment/game implication: overlapping general-purpose governments and service/tax districts require distinct institutional objects; chamber modernization is a time-versioned modular room state.

reports.heading: North Pole city
reports.name: North Pole city
reports.text:
- Current regional planning materials identify North Pole City Council Chambers, 125 Snowman Lane.
- Regional plans can require separate adoption/actions by North Pole City Council, Fairbanks City Council and FNSB Assembly.
Game implication: one regional issue can create parallel agendas/votes in several overlapping governments rather than one `regional government decision`.
